import urllib.request
import urllib.parse
from bs4 import BeautifulSoup
import re
import json

base_url = 'https://bhtcc.netlify.app'

headers = {'User-Agent': 'Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64)'}

visited = set()
to_visit = [base_url]
pages = {}

print("Starting scrape...")

while to_visit:
    curr = to_visit.pop(0)
    # Normalize URL
    parsed = urllib.parse.urlparse(curr)
    # clean fragment
    clean_url = urllib.parse.urlunparse((parsed.scheme, parsed.netloc, parsed.path, '', '', ''))
    if clean_url.endswith('/'):
        clean_url = clean_url[:-1]
    if clean_url in visited:
        continue
    visited.add(clean_url)
    
    print(f"Fetching: {curr}")
    try:
        req = urllib.request.Request(curr, headers=headers)
        with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=10) as resp:
            content_type = resp.headers.get_content_type()
            if 'text/html' not in content_type:
                continue
            html = resp.read().decode('utf-8', errors='ignore')
            pages[curr] = html
            
            # parse links
            soup = BeautifulSoup(html, 'html.parser')
            for a in soup.find_all('a', href=True):
                href = a['href']
                full_url = urllib.parse.urljoin(curr, href)
                parsed_full = urllib.parse.urlparse(full_url)
                if parsed_full.netloc == urllib.parse.urlparse(base_url).netloc:
                    clean_target = urllib.parse.urlunparse((parsed_full.scheme, parsed_full.netloc, parsed_full.path, '', '', ''))
                    if clean_target.endswith('/'):
                        clean_target = clean_target[:-1]
                    if clean_target not in visited and clean_target not in [v.rstrip('/') for v in to_visit]:
                        to_visit.append(full_url)
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"Error fetching {curr}: {e}")

print(f"Scraped {len(pages)} pages.")
with open("scraped_pages.json", "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
    json.dump({"urls": list(pages.keys())}, f, indent=2)

Add-Type -AssemblyName System.Web
$files = Get-ChildItem "C:\Users\amara\.gemini\antigravity\brain\bb026828-c495-42ca-b6b7-042920e4c9a9\scratch\*.html"

foreach ($f in $files) {
    $raw = Get-Content $f.FullName -Raw
    # Extract <main>...</main>
    if ($raw -match '(?s)<main[^>]*>(.*?)</main>') {
        $main = $matches[1]
        # Remove scripts and styles
        $clean = [regex]::Replace($main, '(?s)<(script|style)[^>]*>.*?</\1>', '')
        # Replace tags with space or newline
        $clean = [regex]::Replace($clean, '<(h[1-6]|p|div|li|tr)[^>]*>', "`n`$0")
        $clean = [regex]::Replace($clean, '<[^>]+>', ' ')
        $clean = [System.Web.HttpUtility]::HtmlDecode($clean)
        $clean = [regex]::Replace($clean, '[ \t]+', ' ')
        $clean = [regex]::Replace($clean, '(\r?\n\s*){2,}', "`n`n").Trim()
        
        $outFile = "C:\Users\amara\.gemini\antigravity\brain\bb026828-c495-42ca-b6b7-042920e4c9a9\scratch\" + $f.BaseName + ".txt"
        $clean | Out-File -FilePath $outFile -Encoding utf8
        Write-Host "Processed $($f.Name): $($clean.Length) chars"
    } else {
        Write-Host "No <main> found in $($f.Name)"
    }
}

Our Foundation 
 Our Story & Leadership 
 Ballarat Hindu Temple & Cultural Centre Incorporated (BHTCC) is a community-driven initiative established in 2016 to support the growing regional Hindu diaspora. 

Our Vision 
 To establish and maintain a traditional Hindu Temple and Cultural Centre serving Ballarat and Regional Victoria, creating a peaceful sanctuary that nurtures spiritual growth, cultural heritage, and harmonious multicultural community development. 
 Fostering harmony since 2016 

Our Mission 
 Promote traditional Hindu philosophy, values, and cultural education. 
 Facilitate regular worship, holy festivals, and prayer rituals. 
 Deliver charitable community support services and welfare drives. 
 Foster interfaith cooperation, youth development, and senior engagement. 
 Serving Victoria regional families 

Milestone Journey 
 Interactive Timeline 
 Click on any year to read details about key milestones in our history. 
 2016 2018 2020 2022 2024 2026 

Construction Phase 1 Underway 
 Foundation concrete slabs poured and structural frame erections active. 
 Currently finishing plumbing infrastructure, septic grid installs, and car parking bays. Ganesha Altar stonemasonry is set to begin soon. 
 Local Narrative 
 History of the Hindu Community in Ballarat 
 The Hindu community in Ballarat has grown dynamically over the last two decades. Initially comprising students, healthcare professionals, and information technology workers moving from metropolitan centers, the diaspora has established roots in regional Ballarat, the Golden Plains Shire, and surrounding regions. 
 Without a permanent physical temple, families met in community halls or homes for worship. The formal creation of BHTCC in 2016 gave the community a unified voice, enabling parliamentary recognition, council permits, and the acquisition of the Ross Creek property, ensuring future generations can maintain, celebrate, and preserve their cultural practices in regional Victoria.

# Ballarat Hindu Temple & Cultural Centre (BHTCC)
## Comprehensive Master Documentation & Site Compendium

---

## 1. Executive Summary & Organizational Overview

The **Ballarat Hindu Temple & Cultural Centre Incorporated (BHTCC)** is a community-led initiative founded in 2016 to establish regional Victoria's first major Hindu temple and multipurpose cultural complex. Situated on a serene 5-acre rural property at **110 Vaggs Rd, Ross Creek VIC 3351** (within the Golden Plains Shire, near Ballarat), the project addresses the long-standing spiritual, cultural, educational, and social welfare needs of the expanding Hindu and broader Indian diaspora across western regional Victoria.

The centre integrates traditional Vedic temple architecture designed under Vastu Shastra principles with modern community infrastructure, including a commercial community kitchen, an extensive library and learning classrooms, landscaped meditation gardens, a children’s playground, and ample parking facilities.

```
========================================================================================
                          KEY ORGANIZATIONAL SNAPSHOT
========================================================================================
• Legal Name:               Ballarat Hindu Temple & Cultural Centre Incorporated (BHTCC)
• Entity Type:              Incorporated Association (Victoria, Australia)
• Australian Business No.:  ABN 13 397 829 440
• Tax / Charity Status:     Registered Charity / Not-for-Profit (Advancement of Religion / Community Support)
• Year Established:         2016
• Location:                 110 Vaggs Rd, Ross Creek VIC 3351, Regional Victoria, Australia
• Government Grants:        $900,000+ secured across Victorian State & Federal commitments
• Ground Attendees:         800+ devotees attending landmark ceremonies
• Property Size:            5 Acres in Golden Plains Shire
• Primary Website:          https://bhtcc.netlify.app/
• Primary Contact:          info@ballarathindutemple.org.au | +61 3 5300 0000
========================================================================================
```

---

## 2. Institutional Vision, Mission & Core Values

### 2.1 Vision Statement
> *"To establish and maintain a traditional Hindu Temple and Cultural Centre serving Ballarat and Regional Victoria, creating a peaceful sanctuary that nurtures spiritual growth, cultural heritage, and harmonious multicultural community development."*

### 2.2 Mission Objectives
1. **Philosophical & Cultural Education**: Promote authentic Hindu philosophy, Vedic heritage, values, and cultural education across all generations.
2. **Sacred Worship & Festivals**: Facilitate traditional daily/weekly worship, major holy Hindu festivals, homams, and sacred ceremonies in regional Victoria.
3. **Charitable Welfare & Relief**: Deliver dedicated community support services, crisis relief, dry-ration food drives, and care packages for regional families and local shelters.
4. **Multicultural Harmony & Interfaith Engagement**: Foster intercultural understanding, youth leadership, interfaith collaboration, and senior citizen engagement within the wider Australian society.

---

## 3. History of the Ballarat Hindu Community & Historical Timeline

### 3.1 Historical Narrative
Over the past two decades, regional Ballarat and the surrounding Golden Plains Shire witnessed a steady influx of Indian migrants, originally consisting of international students, healthcare professionals at regional hospitals, information technology consultants, and agricultural entrepreneurs relocating from metropolitan Melbourne and interstate.

Prior to 2016, the regional community lacked a permanent sacred sanctuary, requiring families to rent local municipal halls or host informal poojas and festivals in private residences. In 2016, dedicated community families united to formally incorporate BHTCC, establish legal constitutional bylaws, and secure parliamentary recognition.

### 3.2 Key Historical Milestones (2016 – 2026)

| Year | Milestone Title | Overview & Details |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **2016** | **Formation & Legal Incorporation** | BHTCC was formally founded and officially registered as an Incorporated Association in Victoria (ABN: 13 397 829 440). The community drafted the BHTCC model constitution to establish governance standards. |
| **2018** | **First Major Ganesh Chaturthi Festival** | Inauguration of Ballarat's premier annual multicultural festival. The celebration attracted hundreds of regional residents, winning civic accolades and bridging religious tradition with local community engagement. |
| **2020** | **Ross Creek Land Acquisition** | Secured a 5-acre freehold rural parcel at 110 Vaggs Rd, Ross Creek in the Golden Plains Shire. The parcel was selected for its peaceful natural ambience, aligning with traditional Vastu orientations. |
| **2022** | **Government Funding Commitments** | Secured approximately **$900,000** in combined Victorian State and Federal multicultural capital grants, formally recognized in the Victorian Parliament to support the multipurpose community centre. |
| **2024** | **Bhoomi Pooja & Groundbreaking** | Over 800 devotees, spiritual leaders, and regional dignitaries from Ballarat, Melbourne, and regional Victoria gathered on-site for sacred Vedic groundbreaking poojas. Site earthworks commenced. |
| **2026** | **Construction Phase 1 Underway** | Concrete foundation slabs poured and structural frame erections active. Stormwater management, underground utilities, septic systems, and 75+ parking bays underway; stone shrine construction commencing. |

---

## 4. Governance Board & Executive Leadership

BHTCC is administered with transparent corporate governance by an elected Executive Committee drawn from healthcare, education, civil engineering, and financial sectors:

* **Dr. Harish Kumar – President**
  * *Professional Background*: Healthcare Administration
  * *Role*: Leads strategic vision, government relations, and overall community leadership.
* **Mrs. Priya Rajan – Secretary**
  * *Professional Background*: Secondary Education & Language Program Coordinator
  * *Role*: Oversees community communications, administrative correspondence, language curriculum, and regulatory filings.
* **Mr. Satish Nair – Treasurer**
  * *Professional Background*: Chartered Accountant / Financial Governance Specialist
  * *Role*: Manages financial integrity, statutory audits, donation tracking, and Victorian compliance reports.
* **Mr. Ramesh Patel – Project Manager**
  * *Professional Background*: Civil Engineer / Construction Liaison
  * *Role*: Oversees architectural blueprints, on-site civil works, council permit compliance, and contractor supervision.

---

## 5. The Ross Creek Temple Complex & Architectural Masterplan

The 5-acre Ross Creek complex is master-planned to balance authentic Vedic temple design with practical civic facilities to serve regional Victoria.

```
+---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
|                                ROSS CREEK SITE MASTERPLAN                             |
+---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
|  [Main Car Park Access: 75+ bays] ---> [Main Entrance Lobby & Reception Foyer]         |
|                                                       |                               |
|                                        +--------------v-------------+                 |
|                                        |  PRAYER & MEDITATION HALL  |                 |
|                                        |  (26m x 12m, 350 Capacity) |                 |
|                                        +--------------+-------------+                 |
|                                                       |                               |
|          +-------------------------+------------------+-------------------+           |
|          |                         |                                      |           |
|  +-------v-------+       +---------v---------+                  +---------v--------+  |
|  | Lord Shiva    |       | SRI GANESHA       |                  | Goddess Ambal    |  |
|  | Shrine        |       | MOOLASTHANAM      |                  | Shrine           |  |
|  | (Chandeshwar) |       | (Central Sanctum) |                  | (Sacred Shakti)  |  |
|  +---------------+       +---------+---------+                  +------------------+  |
|                                    |                                                  |
|                        +-----------v----------+                                       |
|                        | Navagraha Mandapam   |                                       |
|                        | (9 Celestial Deities)|                                       |
|                        +----------------------+                                       |
|                                                                                       |
|  [Commercial Kitchen]  <--->  [Library & Classrooms]  <--->  [Gardens & Playground]   |
+---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
```

### 5.1 Comprehensive Facility Breakdown

1. **Sri Ganesha Moolasthanam (Central Sanctum)**
   * *Status*: Under Construction
   * *Description*: The focal point of the temple, constructed from hand-carved solid granite blocks following Shilpa Shastra proportions, dedicated to primary patron deity Lord Ganesha.
2. **Lord Shiva Shrine**
   * *Status*: Planned / Permitted
   * *Description*: Positioned at the north/rear corner (Chandeshwar Sannidhi) in accordance with astronomical planetary coordinates, carved in traditional stone.
3. **Goddess Ambal Shrine**
   * *Status*: Planned / Permitted
   * *Description*: Situated on the left flank of the central Ganesha shrine, dedicated to the Divine Mother, emphasizing feminine energy, empowerment, and Navaratri rituals.
4. **Navagraha Mandapam**
   * *Status*: Planned
   * *Description*: An elevated square stone pavilion housing the nine planetary deities, essential for Vedic planetary pariharas and astrological prayers.
5. **Main Prayer & Meditation Hall**
   * *Status*: Under Construction (Structural framing active)
   * *Dimensions & Capacity*: 26 metres by 12 metres; comfortably accommodates up to 350 devotees for collective bhajans, discourses, and poojas.
6. **Main Entrance Lobby & Foyer**
   * *Status*: Under Construction
   * *Description*: Double-door grand foyer featuring a dedicated shoe room, guest reception desk, digital notices, and welcome orientation area.
7. **Commercial Community Kitchen & Dining Hall**
   * *Status*: Permits Approved (Backed by $400,000 Victorian Government Grant)
   * *Description*: State-of-the-art commercial-grade kitchen equipped for hygienic daily preparation of temple Prasadam (blessed food) and large-scale catering for festivals hosting hundreds of guests.
8. **Spiritual Library & Cultural Classrooms**
   * *Status*: Planned
   * *Description*: Modern learning spaces housing sacred Hindu scriptures, historical texts, youth literature, and classrooms for language teaching and philosophical study.
9. **Landscaped Heritage Gardens & Meditation Paths**
   * *Status*: Planned
   * *Description*: Expansive outdoor retreat planted with traditional sacred flora (Tulsi, flowering trees, neem) and quiet walking tracks for contemplation.
10. **Children's Playground & Family Parklands**
    * *Status*: Planned
    * *Description*: Dedicated safe outdoor play zone equipped for visiting families, youth gatherings, and festival activities.
11. **Main Car Park & Transport Infrastructure**
    * *Status*: Under Construction
    * *Description*: Engineered asphalt and crushed-rock parking surface accommodating over 75 vehicles, including designated accessible bays, bus turnarounds, and safety lighting.

### 5.2 Live Construction Updates
* **Update 1 – Foundation Pours Completed (45% Overall Completion)**:
  * *Date*: 30 May 2026
  * *Milestone*: The primary reinforced concrete foundation slab for the central Ganesh Shrine and structural steel support frames are fully placed.
* **Update 2 – Ground Levelling & Underground Utilities (30% Overall Completion)**:
  * *Date*: 02 April 2026
  * *Milestone*: Heavy site earthmoving, stormwater drainage pipelines, electrical conduit networks, and primary car park access roads successfully completed.

---

## 6. Enshrined Deities & Spiritual Worship

BHTCC is designed to embody authentic Sanatana Dharma traditions while remaining inclusive of all linguistic and regional Hindu traditions across India and the global diaspora.

### 6.1 Central Deities & Sacred Significance

```
========================================================================================
DEITY                   ROLE & ATTRIBUTES                     PRIMARY RITUALS & PLANS
========================================================================================
Lord Ganesha            • Central Primary Deity (Moolasthanam) • Sankatahara Chaturthi Pooja
(Vighnaharta)           • Remover of Obstacles                • Ganapathi Homam
                        • Patron of letters, arts & sciences  • Pradosham services
                        • Represents auspicious beginnings     • Annual Ganesh Chaturthi Festival
                        ----------------------------------------------------------------
                        * Architecture: Hand-carved solid granite sanctuary blocks.

Lord Shiva              • Supreme Transformer & Ascetic Depth • Pradosha Pooja
(Mahadeva)              • Cosmic Dancer (Nataraja)            • Maha Shivaratri (All-night vigil)
                        • Dissolver of spiritual ignorance    • Rudrabhishekam & Bilva Archana
                        ----------------------------------------------------------------
                        * Architecture: North-aligned stone shrine within the prayer hall.

Goddess Ambal           • Divine Mother (Shakti)              • Friday Special Abhishekam
(Devi Parvati/Durga)    • Supreme Cosmic Energy & Nurturing   • Navaratri 9-Night Celebrations
                        • Embodiment of courage and grace     • Lalitha Sahasranama Chanting
                        ----------------------------------------------------------------
                        * Architecture: Gilded stone shrine on the left flank of Ganesha.

Navagrahas              • Nine Celestial Planetary Deities    • Planetary transit poojas
                        • Harmony of cosmic forces            • Shani / Rahu / Ketu remedies
                        ----------------------------------------------------------------
                        * Architecture: Elevated open-air mandapam within hall precinct.
========================================================================================
```

### 6.2 Traditional Priest Booking Services
BHTCC facilitates priest services conducted by qualified Vedic priests for both on-site temple poojas and home blessings across regional Victoria.

* **Available Service Packages**:
  1. *Temple Archana*: Brief personal or family blessing with sacred offering, fruit, and camphor aarti.
  2. *Ganapathi Homam*: Traditional sacred fire ritual invoking Lord Ganesha for auspicious beginnings, new enterprises, and Grihapravesham (housewarmings).
  3. *Satyanarayana Pooja*: Devotional thanksgiving prayer, katha narration, and prasadam offering.
  4. *Milestone & Family Blessings*: Naming ceremonies (Namakarana), first feeding (Annaprashana), birthdays, and wedding anniversaries.
* **Booking System**: Available online via the portal; devotees submit requested pooja type, preferred date, contact information, and home location details.

---

## 7. Community Programs, Education & Social Welfare

Beyond religious worship, BHTCC functions as a vibrant community hub dedicated to cultural education, wellness, and humanitarian outreach.

```
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
|                               REGULAR COMMUNITY PROGRAMS                                |
+-----------------------------+------------------------------------+----------------------+
| PROGRAM TITLE               | SCHEDULE & TIMING                  | TARGET AUDIENCE      |
+-----------------------------+------------------------------------+----------------------+
| Yoga & Meditation Sessions  | Every Saturday                     | All ages & levels    |
|                             | 8:30 AM – 10:00 AM                 | (Free Community)     |
| Sanskrit & Language Classes | Every Sunday                       | Children, youth,     |
|                             | 2:00 PM – 4:00 PM                  | and adults           |
| Seniors Spiritual Gathering | Fortnightly Wednesdays             | Elderly residents &  |
|                             | 11:00 AM – 1:00 PM                 | retirees             |
| Welfare & Food Drives       | Monthly Special Campaigns          | Regional shelters    |
|                             |                                    | & families in need   |
+-----------------------------+------------------------------------+----------------------+
```

### 7.1 Program Details
1. **Yoga & Meditation Sessions**: Weekly mindfulness, Pranayama (breath control), and physical asanas designed to improve physical fitness, mental equilibrium, and spiritual centering.
2. **Sanskrit & Indian Languages Class**: Structured linguistic instruction teaching Sanskrit grammar, sacred stotram chanting, and conversational Hindi and Tamil to preserve linguistic heritage among diaspora youth.
3. **Seniors Spiritual Gathering**: Dedicated social circle offering bhajans, philosophical discussions, fellowship, and warm sattvic lunches to combat social isolation among elderly migrants.
4. **Welfare Outreach & Food Drives**: Monthly charitable drives collecting non-perishable groceries, hot meals, warm blankets, and hygiene kits distributed to local Ballarat emergency shelters and disadvantaged regional families.

---

## 8. Annual Festivals, Calendar of Events & News

### 8.1 Signature Annual Celebrations & Scheduled Events

* **Grand Ganesh Chaturthi Festival**
  * *Date*: 15 September 2026
  * *Time*: 10:00 AM – 8:00 PM
  * *Venue*: BHTCC Ross Creek Site, 110 Vaggs Rd
  * *Category*: Cultural / Major Festival
  * *Program*: Ballarat’s landmark multicultural celebration featuring traditional murti consecration, continuous prayers, cultural classical dance (Bharatanatyam/Kathak), live devotional music, a festive chariot procession, and a community Maha-Prasadam feast.
* **Maha Shivaratri Celebrations**
  * *Date*: 05 March 2026
  * *Time*: 6:00 PM – 6:00 AM (Overnight)
  * *Venue*: BHTCC Site, Ross Creek
  * *Category*: Religious / Devotional
  * *Program*: All-night vigils featuring four prahara abhishekams of the Shiva Lingam, continuous chanting of *Om Namah Shivaya*, Vedic homams, and classical Indian instrumental performances.
* **Yoga & Meditation Workshop**
  * *Date*: 25 June 2026
  * *Time*: 8:30 AM – 10:00 AM
  * *Venue*: Ballarat Community Hub
  * *Category*: Health & Wellness
  * *Program*: An intensive workshop focusing on stress relief, inner clarity, and yogic breathing techniques.

### 8.2 Recent News Announcements & Government Grants
* **Victoria State Government Grants $400k for Community Kitchen (10 May 2026)**: Funding confirmation under Victorian Multicultural Infrastructure grants to engineer a modern regional commercial kitchen and community dining wing.
* **Planning Masterplan Approval Secured for Phase 2 (18 April 2026)**: Formal town planning endorsement granted by the Golden Plains Shire Council approving the multi-use cultural hall, library, and surrounding public parklands.
* **Bhoomi Pooja Ceremony Highlights (12 February 2026)**: Over 800 community members and regional leaders gathered on-site for the groundbreaking ceremony led by Vedic priests.

---

## 9. Membership Structure, Tiers & Benefits

Devotees can support the ongoing operations and long-term capital sustainability of BHTCC through formal membership.

### 9.1 Membership Tiers & Pricing
1. **Ordinary Member**:
   * *Fee*: **$50.00 AUD / Year**
   * *Scope*: Annual membership for individuals wishing to support temple programs.
2. **Association Member**:
   * *Fee*: **$150.00 AUD / Year**
   * *Scope*: Comprehensive annual membership for families, groups, or affiliated community associations.
3. **Life Member**:
   * *Fee*: **$500.00 AUD (One-Time Payment)**
   * *Scope*: Lifetime patron standing with enduring recognition in the temple society.

### 9.2 Member Privileges & Entitlements
* **Full Voting Rights**: Constitutional voting entitlements at BHTCC Annual General Meetings (AGMs) to elect committee members.
* **Priest Service Concessions**: Priority booking scheduling and discounted honorarium rates for priest services.
* **Planning Participation**: Exclusive invitations to contribute to architectural design forums and masterplan working groups.
* **VIP Event Invitations**: Reserved priority seating at annual festivals and civic celebrations.
* **Educational Access**: Free or discounted enrollment for families in yoga workshops and language classes.

---

## 10. Capital Fundraising Campaigns & Pillar Sponsorship

To fund the multi-million dollar construction of the permanent site, BHTCC manages targeted capital appeals and infrastructure sponsorship drives.

```
========================================================================================
CAMPAIGN NAME               FINANCIAL TARGET      FUNDS RAISED TO DATE    PROGRESS
========================================================================================
1. Ganesha Temple Building  $500,000 AUD          $345,000 AUD            69.0%
   * Dedicated to solid granite sanctum, sanctum spires, and sanctum stone masonry.

2. Shiva & Ambal Shrines    $250,000 AUD          $125,000 AUD            50.0%
   * Dedicated to hand-carved stone subsidiary shrines and decorative pilasters.

3. Community Hall & Library $150,000 AUD          $82,000 AUD             54.7%
   * Funding multi-purpose venue, children's park, commercial kitchen, and library.
```

# Ballarat Hindu Temple & Cultural Centre (BHTCC)
## Comprehensive Master Documentation & Site Compendium

> [!NOTE]
> This master document aggregates all content, data records, architectural plans, committee details, and governance policies scraped and synthesized across every page of the [Ballarat Hindu Temple & Cultural Centre Website](https://bhtcc.netlify.app/).

---

## 1. Executive Summary & Organizational Overview

The **Ballarat Hindu Temple & Cultural Centre Incorporated (BHTCC)** is a grassroots community initiative founded in 2016 to create regional Victoria's first major Hindu temple and multipurpose cultural centre. Situated on a serene 5-acre property at **110 Vaggs Rd, Ross Creek VIC 3351** within the Golden Plains Shire, the project serves the spiritual, cultural, educational, and charitable needs of the growing regional Hindu diaspora across Ballarat, Golden Plains, and Western Victoria.

```
========================================================================================
                          KEY ORGANIZATIONAL SNAPSHOT
========================================================================================
• Legal Entity:             Ballarat Hindu Temple & Cultural Centre Incorporated (BHTCC)
• Entity Type:              Incorporated Association (Victoria, Australia)
• Australian Business No.:  ABN 13 397 829 440
• Tax / Charity Status:     Registered Charity / Not-for-Profit (Advancement of Religion / Community Support)
• Year Established:         2016
• Location:                 110 Vaggs Rd, Ross Creek VIC 3351, Regional Victoria, Australia
• Government Grants:        $900,000+ secured across Victorian State & Federal commitments
• Landmark Event Turnout:   800+ devotees attending Bhoomi Pooja and major festivals
• Property Size:            5-Acre Freehold Rural Complex (Golden Plains Shire)
• Official Website:         https://bhtcc.netlify.app/
• Official Contact:         info@ballarathindutemple.org.au | +61 3 5300 0000
========================================================================================
```

---

## 2. Institutional Vision, Mission & Values

### 2.1 Vision Statement
> *"To establish and maintain a traditional Hindu Temple and Cultural Centre serving Ballarat and Regional Victoria, creating a peaceful sanctuary that nurtures spiritual growth, cultural heritage, and harmonious multicultural community development."*

### 2.2 Mission Pillars
1. **Philosophical & Cultural Education**: Foster authentic Hindu philosophy, Vedic heritage, values, and language instruction for youth and families.
2. **Sacred Worship & Festivals**: Facilitate regular traditional worship, sacred homams, daily prasadams, and landmark Hindu festivals in regional Victoria.
3. **Charitable Welfare & Community Support**: Deliver compassionate community relief, dry-ration food drives, blankets, and essential support to Ballarat emergency shelters and regional families experiencing vulnerability.
4. **Multicultural Harmony & Youth Engagement**: Promote interfaith dialogue, active civic collaboration, senior support circles, and youth leadership within regional Australian society.

---

## 3. History of the Ballarat Hindu Community & Milestone Journey

### 3.1 Historical Background
Over the past two decades, the Indian diaspora in Ballarat and surrounding districts grew steadily—initially spearheaded by international university students, medical and healthcare professionals in regional hospitals, IT specialists, and regional business operators moving from metropolitan Melbourne.

Prior to 2016, the absence of a permanent temple required families to gather in rented municipal halls or private residences for poojas. In 2016, community leaders formally organized BHTCC, incorporating under Victorian law to provide an enduring legal foundation, parliamentary advocacy, and land acquisition capability.

### 3.2 Milestone Timeline (2016 – 2026)

```mermaid
timeline
    title BHTCC Historic Milestones
    2016 : Formation & Incorporation : ABN 13 397 829 440 registered : Constitution drafted
    2018 : First Major Ganesh Festival : Annual celebration inaugurated : Regional multicultural staple
    2020 : Ross Creek Land Acquisition : 5-acre rural property secured at 110 Vaggs Rd
    2022 : Government Funding Commitments : $900k+ in State & Federal multicultural grants announced
    2024 : Bhoomi Pooja & Groundbreaking : 800+ devotees attend sacred groundbreaking on-site
    2026 : Construction Phase 1 Active : Foundation slabs poured : Structural steel framing erected
```

* **2016 – Formation & Incorporation**: Established and officially registered as an Incorporated Association in Victoria with legal constitution (ABN: 13 397 829 440).
* **2018 – First Major Ganesh Chaturthi Festival**: Launched Ballarat’s premier multicultural celebration, attracting hundreds of regional residents and bridging diverse communities.
* **2020 – Ross Creek Land Acquisition**: Purchased a 5-acre parcel at 110 Vaggs Rd, Ross Creek in the Golden Plains Shire, chosen for natural serenity and Vastu alignment.
* **2022 – Government Funding Commitments**: Secured ~$900,000 in Victorian State and federal multicultural capital grants, formally acknowledged in parliament.
* **2024 – Bhoomi Pooja & Groundbreaking**: Over 800 devotees from across Victoria participated in Vedic earth-blessing rituals; preliminary civil earthworks commenced.
* **2026 – Construction Phase 1 Underway**: Concrete foundation poured, structural steel frames erected, stormwater infrastructure, septic grids, and parking access roads installed.

### 5.1 Planned Facilities Breakdown

2. **Lord Shiva Shrine**: Carved stone shrine positioned at the north/rear corner in accordance with Vedic cosmological alignment.
3. **Goddess Ambal Shrine**: Dedicated sacred sanctum on the left flank of the Ganesha altar honoring Devi Shakti.
4. **Navagraha Mandapam**: Elevated stone pavilion housing the nine celestial planetary deities.
5. **Main Prayer & Meditation Hall**: Spacious 26m × 12m hall comfortably accommodating up to 350 devotees.
6. **Main Entrance Lobby**: Grand foyer with shoe storage, visitor reception desk, and informational kiosks.
7. **Commercial Community Kitchen**: State-of-the-art facility for daily Prasadams and massive festival banquets (Permits Approved; supported by $400k State Government grant).
8. **Spiritual Library & Classrooms**: Dedicated educational spaces housing holy scriptures and children's language classrooms.
9. **Landscaped Heritage Gardens**: Outdoor meditation tracks, Tulsi enclosures, and shaded seating areas.
10. **Children's Playground**: Safe recreation zone for visiting youth and families.
11. **Main Car Park**: Engineered asphalt/gravel parking area accommodating over 75 vehicles including accessible spaces.

97: 
98: # Add dependencies

import docx
from docx import Document
from docx.shared import Inches, Pt, RGBColor
from docx.enum.text import WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH
from docx.enum.table import WD_TABLE_ALIGNMENT, WD_ALIGN_VERTICAL
from docx.oxml import OxmlElement, parse_xml
from docx.oxml.ns import nsdecls, qn

def set_cell_background(cell, hex_color):
    """Sets background color of a table cell."""
    tc_pr = cell._tc.get_or_add_tcPr()
    shd = parse_xml(f'<w:shd {nsdecls("w")} w:fill="{hex_color}"/>')
    tc_pr.append(shd)

def set_cell_margins(cell, top=120, bottom=120, left=150, right=150):
    """Sets cell padding in twips (1/20 of a pt)."""
    tc_pr = cell._tc.get_or_add_tcPr()
    tc_mar = parse_xml(f'<w:tcMar {nsdecls("w")}><w:top w:w="{top}" w:type="dxa"/><w:bottom w:w="{bottom}" w:type="dxa"/><w:left w:w="{left}" w:type="dxa"/><w:right w:w="{right}" w:type="dxa"/></w:tcMar>')
    tc_pr.append(tc_mar)

def set_table_borders(table, color="D3D3D3", sz="4", val="single"):
    """Sets clean light borders on a table."""
    tbl_pr = table._tbl.tblPr
    borders = parse_xml(f'<w:tblBorders {nsdecls("w")}><w:top w:val="{val}" w:sz="{sz}" w:space="0" w:color="{color}"/><w:bottom w:val="{val}" w:sz="{sz}" w:space="0" w:color="{color}"/><w:left w:val="none"/><w:right w:val="none"/><w:insideH w:val="{val}" w:sz="{sz}" w:space="0" w:color="{color}"/><w:insideV w:val="none"/></w:tblBorders>')
    tbl_pr.append(borders)

def make_callout(doc, text, title="NOTE FOR CLIENT:"):
    tbl = doc.add_table(rows=1, cols=1)
    tbl.alignment = WD_TABLE_ALIGNMENT.CENTER
    tbl.autofit = False
    cell = tbl.cell(0, 0)
    cell.width = Inches(7.0)
    set_cell_background(cell, "FBF8F2")
    set_cell_margins(cell, top=140, bottom=140, left=180, right=180)
    
    # Left border gold
    tc_pr = cell._tc.get_or_add_tcPr()
    borders = parse_xml(f'<w:tcBorders {nsdecls("w")}><w:left w:val="single" w:sz="24" w:space="0" w:color="800000"/><w:top w:val="none"/><w:right w:val="none"/><w:bottom w:val="none"/></w:tcBorders>')
    tc_pr.append(borders)
    
    p = cell.paragraphs[0]
    p.paragraph_format.space_before = Pt(2)
    p.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(2)
    r1 = p.add_run(f"{title} ")
    r1.bold = True
    r1.font.color.rgb = RGBColor(128, 0, 0)
    r1.font.size = Pt(9.5)
    r2 = p.add_run(text)
    r2.font.size = Pt(9.5)
    r2.font.color.rgb = RGBColor(60, 60, 60)

print("Helper functions defined.")

import docx
from docx import Document
from docx.shared import Inches, Pt, RGBColor

from docx.enum.table import WD_TABLE_ALIGNMENT, WD_ALIGN_VERTICAL
from docx.oxml import OxmlElement, parse_xml

def set_cell_background(cell, hex_color):
    tc_pr = cell._tc.get_or_add_tcPr()

    tc_pr.append(shd)

def set_cell_margins(cell, top=100, bottom=100, left=130, right=130):
    tc_pr = cell._tc.get_or_add_tcPr()
    tc_mar = parse_xml(f'<w:tcMar {nsdecls("w")}><w:top w:w="{top}" w:type="dxa"/><w:bottom w:w="{bottom}" w:type="dxa"/><w:left w:w="{left}" w:type="dxa"/><w:right w:w="{right}" w:type="dxa"/></w:tcMar>')
    tc_pr.append(tc_mar)

def set_table_borders(table, color="D3D3D3", sz="4", val="single"):

    borders = parse_xml(f'<w:tblBorders {nsdecls("w")}><w:top w:val="{val}" w:sz="{sz}" w:space="0" w:color="{color}"/><w:bottom w:val="{val}" w:sz="{sz}" w:space="0" w:color="{color}"/><w:left w:val="none"/><w:right w:val="none"/><w:insideH w:val="{val}" w:sz="{sz}" w:space="0" w:color="{color}"/><w:insideV w:val="none"/></w:tblBorders>')
    tbl_pr.append(borders)

def make_callout(doc, text, title="INSTRUCTIONS FOR CLIENT:"):
    tbl = doc.add_table(rows=1, cols=1)

    tbl.autofit = False
    cell = tbl.cell(0, 0)
    cell.width = Inches(7.2)
    set_cell_background(cell, "FAF6F0")
    set_cell_margins(cell, top=140, bottom=140, left=180, right=180)
    
    tc_pr = cell._tc.get_or_add_tcPr()
    borders = parse_xml(f'<w:tcBorders {nsdecls("w")}><w:left w:val="single" w:sz="24" w:space="0" w:color="800000"/><w:top w:val="none"/><w:right w:val="none"/><w:bottom w:val="none"/></w:tcBorders>')
    tc_pr.append(borders)
    
    p = cell.paragraphs[0]
    p.paragraph_format.space_before = Pt(2)
    p.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(2)
    r1 = p.add_run(f"{title} ")

    r1.font.color.rgb = RGBColor(128, 0, 0)
    r1.font.name = "Arial"
    r1.font.size = Pt(9.5)
    r2 = p.add_run(text)
    r2.font.name = "Arial"
    r2.font.size = Pt(9.5)
    r2.font.color.rgb = RGBColor(60, 60, 60)
    doc.add_paragraph().paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(4)

def add_heading_1(doc, text):
    h = doc.add_paragraph()
    h.paragraph_format.space_before = Pt(16)
    h.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(6)
    h.paragraph_format.keep_with_next = True
    r = h.add_run(text)
    r.bold = True
    r.font.name = "Arial"
    r.font.size = Pt(13)
    r.font.color.rgb = RGBColor(128, 0, 0)
    return h

def create_styled_table(doc, headers, rows_data):
    table = doc.add_table(rows=len(rows_data) + 1, cols=len(headers))
    table.alignment = WD_TABLE_ALIGNMENT.CENTER
    table.autofit = False
    set_table_borders(table, color="DCD6CD", sz="4")
    
    col_widths = [Inches(1.4), Inches(1.8), Inches(2.6), Inches(1.4)]
    
    # Header row
    hdr_cells = table.rows[0].cells
    for i, header_text in enumerate(headers):
        cell = hdr_cells[i]
        cell.width = col_widths[i]
        set_cell_background(cell, "6B1D2F") # Deep Maroon
        set_cell_margins(cell, top=120, bottom=120, left=120, right=120)
        p = cell.paragraphs[0]
        p.alignment = WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.LEFT
        p.paragraph_format.space_before = Pt(0)
        p.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(0)
        run = p.add_run(header_text)
        run.bold = True
        run.font.name = "Arial"
        run.font.size = Pt(9)
        run.font.color.rgb = RGBColor(255, 255, 255)
    
    # Repeat header row across pages
    trPr = table.rows[0]._tr.get_or_add_trPr()
    trPr.append(parse_xml(f'<w:tblHeader {nsdecls("w")}/>'))
    
    # Data rows
    for r_idx, row_data in enumerate(rows_data):
        row_cells = table.rows[r_idx + 1].cells
        bg_color = "FFFFFF" if r_idx % 2 == 0 else "FAF8F5"
        for c_idx, cell_value in enumerate(row_data):
            cell = row_cells[c_idx]
            cell.width = col_widths[c_idx]
            set_cell_background(cell, bg_color)
            set_cell_margins(cell, top=100, bottom=100, left=120, right=120)
            p = cell.paragraphs[0]
            p.alignment = WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.LEFT
            p.paragraph_format.space_before = Pt(0)
            p.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(0)
            
            # Format fillable field specially
            if c_idx == 2:
                # Client Input cell
                run = p.add_run(cell_value)
                run.font.name = "Arial"
                run.font.size = Pt(9)
                if cell_value.startswith("[ ]") or cell_value.startswith("[___"):
                    run.font.color.rgb = RGBColor(80, 80, 80)
                else:
                    run.font.color.rgb = RGBColor(20, 20, 20)
            elif c_idx == 0:
                # Parameter Name
                run = p.add_run(cell_value)
                run.bold = True
                run.font.name = "Arial"
                run.font.size = Pt(8.5)
                run.font.color.rgb = RGBColor(107, 29, 47)
            elif c_idx == 1:
                # Existing Site Value
                run = p.add_run(cell_value)
                run.font.name = "Arial"
                run.font.size = Pt(8.5)
                run.font.color.rgb = RGBColor(70, 70, 70)
            else:
                # Developer Guidance
                run = p.add_run(cell_value)
                run.font.name = "Arial"
                run.font.size = Pt(8)
                run.font.color.rgb = RGBColor(110, 110, 110)
    
    doc.add_paragraph().paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(8)
    return table
